common.propsOffWarning: Remove all propellers before connecting the battery.

demo.title: Demo mode.
demo.bodySome: Some features are simulated: this app version cannot do them on a real flight controller yet, so nothing is read from or written to the board for them.
demo.bodyAll: Everything runs on a simulated flight controller. Nothing is read from or written to a real board.

welcome.title: Welcome
welcome.body: This wizard flashes Betaflight and configures your flight controller step by step, no website needed.

connect.title: Connect
connect.description: Plug the flight controller into the computer with a USB data cable.

firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.description: Check that the board runs a recent Betaflight version, and update it if needed.

components.title: What is connected?
components.description: Tell us what is wired to the flight controller. We only ask about the parts you have.

receiver.title: Receiver
receiver.description: The receiver gets the commands from your radio.

binding.title: Binding
binding.description: Pair the receiver with your transmitter.

vtx.title: Video transmitter
vtx.description: Lets the flight controller change video channel and power from your radio or goggles.

gps.title: GPS
gps.description: Used for rescue mode and position on the OSD.

esc.title: ESC & motors
esc.description: How the flight controller talks to the motors.

switches.title: Switches
switches.description: Choose which switch on your radio arms the quad and turns on flight modes.

review.title: Review
review.description: Check everything before it is written to the board. Nothing has been changed yet.

apply.title: Apply
apply.description: Write the settings to the flight controller and check that they stuck.

welcome.need1: The flight controller, with all propellers removed.
welcome.need2: A USB cable that carries data (not a charge-only cable).
welcome.need3: Your radio, bound to the receiver, if you have one.

connect.step1: Plug in the flight controller. Do not connect the battery.
connect.step2: Choose it in the list, or let the wizard find it.
connect.dfuTitle: The board is in flashing (DFU) mode
connect.dfuBody: It can be flashed, but not configured, in this mode. Continue to the firmware step, or unplug and replug it to start it normally.
connect.driverHelpTitle: The board does not show up?
connect.driverHelp1: Try another cable or USB port. Many cables only charge.
connect.driverHelp2: On Windows a driver may be missing. The wizard can install it for you.

firmware.unsupportedTitle: This firmware is too old for the wizard
firmware.unsupportedBody: The wizard supports Betaflight {min} and newer. Update the firmware to continue.
firmware.upToDate: Your firmware is up to date.
firmware.releasesUnavailable: The list of versions is not available offline. You can keep the current firmware.
firmware.releasesFailed: Could not load the list of versions.
firmware.backupNote: Your current settings are backed up before the update.
firmware.doNotUnplug: Do not unplug the board until this finishes.

readProtect.title: This board is locked (read protection)
readProtect.what: The chip on this flight controller has read protection turned on. Some boards ship like this from the factory, or after someone used other flashing tools. While it is on, new firmware cannot be written.
readProtect.why: Nothing has been changed on the board so far.
readProtect.eraseWarning: Removing the protection ERASES THE WHOLE CHIP. This cannot be undone.
readProtect.lose1: The current firmware is deleted. The board will not fly until the new firmware is flashed, which the wizard does right after.
readProtect.lose2: All settings stored on the board are deleted.
readProtect.backupSaved: A backup of your settings was saved before the update. You can restore it from Backups.
readProtect.noBackup: No backup of the board's settings could be saved, so they cannot be restored afterwards.
readProtect.safe: This is the normal way to unlock a board and does not damage it. Keep the USB cable plugged in until flashing is finished.
readProtect.understand: I understand that everything on the chip will be erased.
readProtect.erase: Erase the chip and continue flashing
readProtect.leave: Don't want to erase it? Unplug the board. Nothing on it has been changed.

rxKindHint.SERIAL: For example ExpressLRS, Crossfire, TBS, FrSky or FlySky receivers.
rxKindHint.SPI: Your board reports a built-in ExpressLRS receiver.
rxKindHint.NONE: You need a receiver to fly. You can come back later.

vtxKindHint.DIGITAL: Shows the OSD in your goggles.
vtxKindHint.ANALOG: Change channel and power from the OSD menu.
vtxKindHint.NONE: The video transmitter is not connected to a UART.

components.gpsHint: Enables GPS rescue and position on the OSD.
components.escTelemetryHint: Only if a telemetry wire from the ESC goes to a UART. Not needed with bidirectional DShot.
components.softSerialNote: Soft serial ports are not supported in this version.

receiver.telemetryQuestion: Send telemetry (battery, signal) back to the radio?
receiver.telemetryHint: Telemetry shows battery voltage and link quality on your radio.
receiver.elrsHint: With ExpressLRS, the arm switch must be on AUX1.
receiver.onboardBody: No UART is needed. Bind it to your radio after setup.

binding.familyQuestion: Which radio system is this receiver?
binding.crossfireNote: Crossfire and Tracer receivers are bound from the transmitter's TBS menu (or TBS Agent). There is nothing to set here.
binding.what: ExpressLRS pairs the receiver with your transmitter using a binding phrase: a word or sentence you choose, a bit like a Wi-Fi password.
binding.mustMatch: It must be exactly the same as the phrase on your transmitter: same letters, capitals and spaces. Otherwise they will not connect.
binding.whereToFind: You set it when the transmitter's ExpressLRS module was flashed (for example in ExpressLRS Configurator). If you don't know it, choose the bind button instead.
binding.howQuestion: How do you want to bind?
binding.useButton: Skip the phrase and bind with the button
binding.phraseLabel: Binding phrase (same as on your transmitter)
binding.spacesWarning: The phrase starts or ends with a space. That is allowed, but it must be the same on the transmitter.
binding.notSaved: The phrase is not saved anywhere. The app turns it into a short code for the receiver and then forgets it.
binding.phraseSet: Binding phrase set. It will be written to the flight controller when you apply the settings. The phrase itself was not saved.
binding.uartPhrase: This receiver is connected with wires and keeps its own binding phrase. The flight controller cannot change it, so set the same phrase on the receiver itself:
binding.uartPhrase1: In ExpressLRS Configurator, enter the phrase when you flash the receiver, or
binding.uartPhrase2: Turn on the receiver's Wi-Fi (ExpressLRS Lua script on the transmitter: WiFi Connectivity → Enable Rx WiFi) and enter the phrase on its web page.
binding.buttonSpi1: Put the flight controller's receiver in bind mode: press its bind button (see the board's manual; it is not the BOOT button), or use Bind on the Receiver tab of the Betaflight app.
binding.buttonUart1: Put the receiver in bind mode: plug the quad in and unplug it three times in a row (each time less than a second), or press the button on the receiver. Its light blinks twice quickly.
binding.button2: On the transmitter, open the ExpressLRS Lua script and choose Bind.
binding.button3: When the light on the receiver stays on, it is bound.
binding.buttonSpiKeep: The wizard keeps the board's current binding. You can bind after applying the settings.
binding.buttonLater: You can do this any time after the wizard is finished.

vtx.digitalHint: Digital systems use MSP DisplayPort for the OSD.

gps.hint: Most modules use UBLOX. Wire GPS TX to the UART RX pad and GPS RX to TX.

esc.bidirHint: Needs ESC firmware that supports it (BLHeli_32, Bluejay, AM32).
esc.polesHint: Count the magnets on the motor bell. Most 5 inch motors have 14.
esc.propsOutHint: Only if your frame setup uses props out.
esc.reverseHint: Changing the spin direction of one motor will be added later.

motorTest.title: Motor test
motorTest.warning: Motors can spin. Confirm both before testing:
motorTest.ackBattery: The battery is disconnected. The board is on USB power only.
motorTest.ackBatteryHint: Many ESCs cannot spin motors on USB power. That is expected and safe.
motorTest.unavailable: The motor test is not available in this version yet. You can skip it and check the motors later in Betaflight Configurator, with the propellers removed.
motorTest.diagram: Motor layout, seen from above, front at the top
motorTest.running: Motor {n} is spinning. Select it again or Stop to stop it.
motorTest.usbOnlyNote: Motors stop when you leave this step or switch windows, when you close the window or quit the app, and on their own within half a second if the app stops responding.
motorTest.orderOk: The right motor spins for each button.
motorTest.directionOk: Every motor spins in the direction shown.

batteryChecks.title: Checks that need the battery
batteryChecks.warning: These checks need the battery connected, so they are turned off in this version. Do them later with the propellers removed.
batteryChecks.esc: ESC check and motor direction under battery power

switches.namesNew: Mode names for Betaflight {version} and newer.
switches.liveHint: Flip the switches on your radio: the active mode lights up.
switches.liveUnavailable: Live switch display is not available yet. Choose the switches from the lists.
switches.liveStopped: The live switch display stopped. Check the connection.
switches.armHint: Arming starts the motors. Use a switch that is hard to flip by accident.

review.clearingsTitle: These ports will be cleared first
review.noClearings: No existing port settings will be cleared.
review.clearingsHint: Only roles the wizard manages are removed. Other port settings stay as they are.
review.nothingWritten: Nothing is written until you select Apply on the next step.
review.planUnavailableTitle: This app version cannot apply settings yet
review.planUnavailableBody: The board connection in this version can only show a preview of the changes, so Apply is turned off. Update the app to apply settings. Nothing has been changed on the board.
review.clearingsUnknown: The ports that will be cleared are shown once the board can prepare the exact changes.

apply.doNotUnplug: Do not unplug the board until this finishes.
apply.verifying: Checking the settings on the board…
apply.verified: All settings were saved and checked.
apply.notSaved: The settings were sent but not saved. Nothing changed on the board.
apply.failedHint: A backup was made before applying. You can restore it below.

mismatch.title: Some settings did not stick
mismatch.body: The board was read back after saving, and these values are different:
mismatch.step1: Select Apply again. A second try often fixes it.
mismatch.step2: If the same setting fails again, your firmware may not support it. Update the firmware and try again.
mismatch.step3: You can restore the backup below to undo all changes.

apply.notReconnected: The settings were saved, but the board did not reconnect by itself. Unplug the USB cable, plug it back in, and connect again to check them.

done.next1: Bind your receiver to your radio if you have not already.
done.next2: Check that the arm switch and modes react on your radio.
done.next3: Do a short hover test outdoors, away from people.
done.linkIssues: Report a problem with the wizard

backups.title: Backups
backups.intro: Backups for this board, newest first.
backups.sessionOnly: Backups made in this session. Older backups are in the backups folder.
backups.folderFallback: The folder could not be opened. It is here:
backups.confirmBody: All settings on the board are replaced with the backup from {date}. The board restarts.

ports.noneFree: No free port. Free one up on another step, or check the wiring.

question.receiver: Which UART is the receiver wired to?
question.vtx: Which UART is the video transmitter wired to?
question.gps: Which UART is the GPS wired to?
question.escTelemetry: Which UART is the ESC telemetry wire on?

wiring.receiver: Receiver TX goes to the UART RX pad, receiver RX to TX.
wiring.vtx: The VTX control wire goes to the UART TX pad.
wiring.gps: GPS TX goes to the UART RX pad, GPS RX to TX.
wiring.escTelemetry: The ESC telemetry wire goes to the UART RX pad.

reason.softserial_mvp: Soft serial is not supported yet

links.fallback: Open this address in your browser:

validation.firmwareUnsupported: Update the firmware to Betaflight {min} or newer.
validation.firmwareDecide: Choose to update or keep the current firmware.
validation.noConfig: The board did not report its ports. Reconnect and try again.
validation.receiverRequired: Choose a receiver. You need one to fly.
validation.noOnboardReceiver: This board has no built-in receiver.
validation.vtxProtocolRequired: Choose how the video transmitter is controlled.
validation.portConflict: {role}: {port} cannot be used. Choose another port.
validation.bidirNeedsDshot: Bidirectional DShot needs a DShot protocol.
validation.motorPolesInvalid: Motor poles must be an even number between 2 and 64.
validation.armAlwaysOn: The arm switch needs an off position.
validation.armOverlap: Arm and {mode} use the same switch position.
validation.modeUnknown: {mode} is not a mode this wizard can set.
validation.modeNeedsFirmware: {mode} needs Betaflight {version} or newer. Remove it or update the firmware.
validation.elrsArmAux1: With ExpressLRS, arm must be on AUX1.
validation.modeRangeInvalid: The switch position for {mode} is not valid.
validation.auxInvalid: The switch channel for {mode} is not valid.
validation.notGenerated: Wait for the preview to finish.
validation.notApplied: Apply the settings and wait for the check to finish.
validation.planUnavailable: This app version cannot apply settings yet. Update the app.
validation.crsfFamilyRequired: Choose which radio system the receiver uses.
validation.bindingRequired: Choose how to bind the receiver.
validation.phraseNotSet: Enter the binding phrase and press “Use this phrase”, or bind with the button.

BOARD_NOT_FOUND.title: No flight controller found
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.body: The computer does not see a flight controller. This is usually the cable or the USB port.
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.step1: Unplug the USB cable and plug it back in. Wait a few seconds.
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.step2: Try another cable. Many USB cables only charge.
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.step3: Plug straight into the computer, not through a hub.
BOARD_NOT_FOUND.step4: Check that a light turns on on the board. If nothing lights up, it is not getting power.

PORT_BUSY.title: The flight controller's connection is in use
PORT_BUSY.body: Another program, or another window of this app, has the connection open.
PORT_BUSY.step1: Close other windows of this app, and apps such as Betaflight Configurator or Cura.
PORT_BUSY.step2: Unplug and replug the board, then try again.

PORT_BUSY_APP.title: This app is already using the flight controller
PORT_BUSY_APP.body: Another window of this app, or a task still running here (such as a motor test or the live switch check), has the connection.
PORT_BUSY_APP.step1: Close the other window of this app, or finish what it is doing.

PORT_BUSY_EXTERNAL.title: Another program is using the flight controller
PORT_BUSY_EXTERNAL.body: Another app on this computer has the connection open.
PORT_BUSY_EXTERNAL.step1: Close Betaflight Configurator, Cura or another app that may use the port (for example ESC Configurator or a 3D-printer tool).
PORT_BUSY_EXTERNAL.step2: Unplug and replug the board, then try again.

DISCONNECTED.title: The flight controller was disconnected
DISCONNECTED.body: The connection to the board was lost.
DISCONNECTED.step1: Check that the USB cable is firmly plugged in.
DISCONNECTED.step2: Select Reconnect. Your answers so far are kept.

TIMEOUT.title: The flight controller stopped responding
TIMEOUT.body: The board did not answer in time.
TIMEOUT.step1: Check the cable, then select Try again.
TIMEOUT.step2: If it keeps happening, unplug and replug the board.

SERIAL_ERROR.title: Could not talk to the board
SERIAL_ERROR.body: The USB connection reported an error.
SERIAL_ERROR.step2: Try another USB port or cable.

DRIVER_MISSING.title: Windows needs a driver for this board
DRIVER_MISSING.body: Windows sees the board but has no driver for it. This is common on a new computer.
DRIVER_MISSING.step1: Select Install the driver. It takes a minute.
DRIVER_MISSING.step2: Unplug and replug the board, then try again.

USB_ERROR.title: USB error
USB_ERROR.body: The computer reported a USB problem while talking to the board.
USB_ERROR.step2: Try another USB port, straight on the computer.

UNSUPPORTED_FIRMWARE.title: This firmware is not supported
UNSUPPORTED_FIRMWARE.body: The wizard only sets up recent Betaflight versions.
UNSUPPORTED_FIRMWARE.step1: Go to the firmware step and update.

MSP_UNSUPPORTED.title: The board does not support this
MSP_UNSUPPORTED.body: The firmware on the board does not know this request.
MSP_UNSUPPORTED.step1: Update the firmware and try again.

MSP_BAD_RESPONSE.title: Unexpected answer from the board
MSP_BAD_RESPONSE.body: The board sent an answer the wizard did not understand.
MSP_BAD_RESPONSE.step1: Try again. If it repeats, reconnect the board.

CLI_ERROR.title: The board rejected a command
CLI_ERROR.body: A settings command failed on the board. The board message is shown below.
CLI_ERROR.step1: Try again. If the same command fails, report the problem.

DFU_NOT_FOUND.title: The board did not enter flashing mode
DFU_NOT_FOUND.body: The board restarts into a special mode (DFU) to install firmware. It did not show up in that mode.
DFU_NOT_FOUND.step2: If that fails, the DFU driver may be missing. Select Install the driver.
DFU_NOT_FOUND.step3: Or unplug the board, hold the BOOT button, plug it in while holding it, then release.

FLASH_FAILED.title: The firmware install did not finish
FLASH_FAILED.body: Something interrupted the install. The board is not damaged and you can flash again.
FLASH_FAILED.step1: Leave the board plugged in and do not touch the cable.
FLASH_FAILED.step3: If it fails again, try another cable and port.

VERIFY_MISMATCH.title: The firmware check failed
VERIFY_MISMATCH.body: The firmware read back from the board does not match what was written.
VERIFY_MISMATCH.step1: Select Flash again with full erase.
VERIFY_MISMATCH.step2: If it fails again, try another cable and port.

READ_PROTECTED.title: The board is read protected
READ_PROTECTED.body: The chip is locked, so new firmware cannot be written. Nothing was erased.
READ_PROTECTED.step1: Removing the lock erases the whole chip, including all settings. The wizard asks before doing it.
READ_PROTECTED.step2: If you are unsure, unplug the board and ask for help.

REPLUG_REQUIRED.title: Unplug and replug the board
REPLUG_REQUIRED.body: The board needs a fresh start to continue.
REPLUG_REQUIRED.step1: Unplug the USB cable, wait 3 seconds and plug it back in.

FIRMWARE_TOO_LARGE.title: The firmware does not fit
FIRMWARE_TOO_LARGE.body: This firmware is too large for the board.
FIRMWARE_TOO_LARGE.step1: Choose another version, or report the problem.

INVALID_FIRMWARE.title: The firmware file is not valid
INVALID_FIRMWARE.body: The firmware file is damaged or not for this board.
INVALID_FIRMWARE.step1: Try again. The file is downloaded again.

NO_FLASH_LAYOUT.title: Unknown memory layout
NO_FLASH_LAYOUT.body: The wizard does not know how to flash this chip.
NO_FLASH_LAYOUT.step1: Report the problem with the technical details.

NETWORK_ERROR.title: No internet connection
NETWORK_ERROR.body: The wizard could not reach the Betaflight servers.
NETWORK_ERROR.step1: Check that the computer is online.

BUILD_API_ERROR.title: The build server had a problem
BUILD_API_ERROR.body: The Betaflight build server returned an error.
BUILD_API_ERROR.step1: Wait a minute and try again.

BUILD_FAILED.title: The firmware build failed
BUILD_FAILED.body: The build server could not build firmware for this board. The server message is shown below.
BUILD_FAILED.step1: Choose another version, or report the problem.

IO_ERROR.title: Could not read or write a file
IO_ERROR.body: A file on this computer could not be read or written.
IO_ERROR.step1: Check that the disk is not full, then try again.

DATA_ERROR.title: Unexpected data
DATA_ERROR.body: Some data could not be read.
DATA_ERROR.step1: Try again. If it repeats, report the problem.

MOTOR_TEST_REFUSED.title: The motor test was not started
MOTOR_TEST_REFUSED.body: Safety checks stopped the motor test. The reason is shown below.
MOTOR_TEST_REFUSED.step1: Confirm that the propellers are removed and the battery is disconnected.

BOARD_ARMED.title: The board is armed
BOARD_ARMED.body: Motors cannot be tested while the board is armed.
BOARD_ARMED.step1: Flip the arm switch on your radio to off.

MOTOR_TEST_NOT_ACTIVE.title: The motor test stopped
MOTOR_TEST_NOT_ACTIVE.body: The motors stopped on their own, for safety.
MOTOR_TEST_NOT_ACTIVE.step1: Start the test again if needed.

CANCELLED.title: Cancelled
CANCELLED.step1: Start it again when you are ready.

BUSY.title: Please wait
BUSY.step1: Wait for it to finish, then try again.

INVALID_ARGUMENT.title: Invalid request
INVALID_ARGUMENT.body: The wizard sent something the app could not use.
INVALID_ARGUMENT.step1: Report the problem with the technical details.

INTERNAL.title: Something went wrong
INTERNAL.body: An unexpected error happened in the app.
INTERNAL.step1: Report the problem with the technical details.

NOT_IMPLEMENTED.title: Not available yet
NOT_IMPLEMENTED.body: This part of the app is not finished yet.
NOT_IMPLEMENTED.step1: You can skip it for now.

UNKNOWN.title: Something went wrong
UNKNOWN.step1: Try again. If it repeats, report the problem.

CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED.title: The board cannot use part of this setup
CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED.body: The flight controller does not support something you chose, most often the receiver type.
CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED.step1: Go back to Components and choose a different receiver, for example one wired to a UART.
CONFIG_UNSUPPORTED.step2: If the board has a built-in receiver and you still see this, report the problem and include the details below.

driverReplace.title: Installing the driver replaces another driver
driverReplace.body: {device} currently uses the {driver} driver. Installing the WinUSB driver replaces it, so this app and Betaflight can flash the board.
driverReplace.tools: Programs that rely on the old driver may stop seeing the board in bootloader mode, for example STM32CubeProgrammer or DfuSe with ST's STTub30 driver.
driverReplace.undo: If you need those programs again, reinstall their driver from their installer. Nothing changes on the flight controller itself.
driverReplace.understand: I understand that the {driver} driver will be replaced by WinUSB.
